justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain Linkage in R6 core as a deprecated or retired compatibility resource while discouraging new use.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 instances and generated surfaces, but keeps a trial-use/FMM 0 arbitrary-resource linkage model in core and may require indefinite validator/API support.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal of retiring a very low-maturity broad linkage resource is reasonable: R4 `Linkage` was trial-use/FMM 0, and the R6 package contains no `Linkage` StructureDefinition. The break is severe and the local inputs do not include the official rationale, so the removal is not conclusively justified. However, the true less-breaking base alternative would materially undercut the cleanup by keeping the old resource identity in R6 core, so the breaking design is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would have kept the same `resourceType: Linkage` and R4 element shape in R6 with a deprecated or retired status and clear guidance not to use it for new content. That is a real base-design alternative, unlike an external profile, local extension, or conversion script. It is only partial because R6 implementations would still need validators, parsers, generated classes, endpoints, and conformance metadata for a low-maturity arbitrary-resource equivalence model that may never disappear.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the R4 Linkage content model inside a deprecated R6 Linkage resource; profiles, extensions, or ConceptMaps alone are migration mitigations.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Avoids field-level data loss, but preserves broad ambiguous arbitrary-resource linkage semantics and can compete with Patient.link or domain-specific relationship mechanisms.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R4 `active`, `author`, `item.type`, `item.resource`, and `lnk-1` model has no standard R6 destination in the supplied package. Removing that low-maturity arbitrary-resource assertion model is a plausible R6 goal, and if the resource is retired the loss of its local content model follows. Because there is no official rationale or endorsed successor in the local inputs, this remains only probably justified, not proven.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have kept `Linkage.active`, `Linkage.author`, `Linkage.item`, `Linkage.item.type`, and `Linkage.item.resource` on a deprecated R6 `Linkage` resource. That would preserve most R4-valid content better than a ConceptMap, external profile, or extension-only strategy. It is partial because it would keep a general-purpose linkage assertion in the base resource registry, create ongoing validation and API burden, and risk ambiguous or duplicate relationship channels alongside more specific R6 mechanisms.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the LinkageType CodeSystem and ValueSet in R6 as retired or historical terminology for validation and migration.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Low to moderate tradeoff: a small dormant legacy terminology remains visible, but terminology resolution and enum generation for preserved Linkage data continue to work.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Removing terminology used only by a removed resource is understandable, but the R4 LinkageType system is small and self-contained. Keeping it as retired terminology would not require restoring the `Linkage` resource, endpoint, or content model, and would still support compatibility layers and historical validation. On the local evidence, the terminology removal appears more avoidable than the resource removal itself.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The backward-compatible base design would keep `http://hl7.org/fhir/linkage-type` and `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/linkage-type` in the R6 package with retired or historical status and notes that no current R6 base element binds to them. This is a base-package alternative, not merely conversion tooling. It would let validators, generators, extensions, and migration guides continue to refer to the canonical R4 role codes `source`, `alternate`, and `historical`.
